seo_001: You can recognise it by its massive trunk, fused from several stems, with club-shaped aerial roots hanging from the lower branches. It stands in the Munmyo shrine courtyard, at Sungkyunkwan.
seo_002: You can recognise it by its twisting, propped and cabled trunk, missing one whole limb, its surviving eastern branch spiralling upward like a coil. It stands along the palace path at Changdeokgung.
seo_003: You can recognise it by the drooping yuju growths on its branches and the low fence keeping visitors just outside the root area. It stands on Madeul-ro, facing the hillside grave of Yeonsangun.
seo_004: You can recognise it by its bark, flaking into pale patches until whole sections look bone white, and its trunk splitting near the ground into what looks like two pines. It stands beside the Constitutional Court on Bukchon-ro.
seo_006: You can recognise it by its huge trunk splitting into four massive limbs, braced with metal supports, and six younger zelkovas grown up around it. It stands in a small green space in Hwayang-dong.
seo_007: You can recognise it by its thick, deeply corked bark and wide branch spread reaching nearly ten metres each way. It stands barely ten metres from the wall of Geonyoung Apartment Complex 2.
